panels.rationale: The panel is a clinical photograph of the mouth of a young adult with Rett syndrome, showing marked dental decay and tooth erosion. Tooth erosion is consistent with bruxism, a core manifestation of Rett syndrome, and the caption specifically documents erosion of multiple teeth. The article is a case report focused on Rett syndrome, supporting disease attribution.

in_text_mentions: Fifteen months later, the patient presented with increasing pain and agitation. The broad differential for her increased pain and agitation was reconsidered, and the family’s goals of care were re-explored. Her physical exam was normal for her except for her oral exam which revealed visible caries and tooth erosion, without significant gingival erythema (Figures 1, 2).

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 5 panels (a, b, c, d, e). a: Intraoral maxillary occlusal photograph of a patient with Rett syndrome, showing dental findings described in the text; real patient clinical photo, no vocabulary-matched findings but proposed dental manifestations. b: Intraoral mandibular occlusal photograph of a patient with Rett syndrome, showing macroglossia, gingivitis and dental caries described in the text; real patient clinical photo. c: Right lateral intraoral photograph of a Rett syndrome patient showing malocclusion and anterior open bite described in the text; real patient clinical photo. d: Left lateral intraoral photograph of a Rett syndrome patient showing malocclusion and anterior open bite described in the text; real patient clinical photo. e: Frontal intraoral photograph of a Rett syndrome patient showing anterior open bite, malocclusion, gingivitis and dental caries described in the text; real patient clinical photo.

in_text_mentions: In regard to her dental examination, extraoral examination was insignificant. The patient had symmetrical face, and the lips were incompetent and dry. On the other hand, her intraoral examination was remarkable. Soft tissue examination showed normal alveolar mucosa, macroglossia, with generalized gingivitis with no abnormality in the floor of the mouth. The hard tissue examination showed mixed dentition stage matching chronological age, generalized enamel hypomineralization, multiple carious teeth, malocclusion, and anterior open bite (Figure 1).
